text:
jamie: Heads up — seeing a silent BMC reboot wave across eu-west3 racks after last night's maintenance. ~120 nodes cycled over ~15m, many stuck provisioning and failing GPU alloc. Jobs are piling in the queue. :grimacing:
ashok: ack. Any obvious BMC firmware id?
maria: we pushed bmc-fw v2.7.4 at 02:00 UTC. change log mentions 'secure-boot flag default change' + watchdog tuning.
lee: hmm secure-boot toggles shouldn't cause reboots, but watchdog tuning could. Do you have SOL logs or chassis status?
jamie: grabbing a short snippet from one affected host: ```
Apr 03 02:12:03 bmc kernel: watchdog: BMC triggered reset
Apr 03 02:12:03 bmc ipmi: chassis power down
Apr 03 02:12:06 bmc ipmi: chassis power up
Apr 03 02:12:15 provisioning: pxe boot timeout, tftp retry
```
ashok: that looks like an in-band watchdog flip on the BMC side. Could be a default watchdog timeout lowered in v2.7.4.
maria: change-log snippet we shipped: "adjust watchdog default to 2m to improve cold-boot recovery; enable secure-boot flag on BMC attach by default" — I can paste full note if needed.
lee: if BMC is rebooting, PXE sessions drop and provisioner retries, which explains GPU alloc backpressure. Any spike in provisioning retries / scheduler backpressure metrics?
jamie: yes — GPU allocation queue length spiked from ~200 to ~2.1k in 18m and autoscaler started shifting overflow to burst cloud capacity (estimate +$2.5k/hr so far).
oncall-bot: incident severity P1 created (id: INC-2026-043). Assigned: eng-oncall.
ashok: prioritizing: 1) stop propagation (prevent further BMC reboots), 2) restore capacity on a subset of racks, 3) rollout rollback or fast hotfix.
maria: we have two options: push a hotfix that disables the updated watchdog default via BMC config (non-disruptive on some models) or roll back the firmware image. Rollback will require a BMC flash which is disruptive too.
lee: can we set watchdog to disabled via IPMI without reflashing? If yes, do a canary. Command I'm thinking: `ipmitool raw 0x06 0x57 0x01 0x00` (example) — test on a single node first.
jamie: tested on rack eu-west3-r05 (12 nodes) — ran ipmitool disable-watchdog on one node, it stopped rebooting, provisioning resumed for that node. :thumbsup:
ashok: good. Action: run a targeted config change on canary racks (r05/r06) to disable watchdog default. If that stabilizes, we can roll forward config rather than a full rollback.
maria: I'm prepping an automated job to set the flag via our fleet mgmt (will use `bmcctl set watchdog=off`). Will target 2 racks at a time. ETA ~10m.
jamie: note: two node models (BMC-vX / mfg-abc) do not accept config via bmcctl — they'll need a flash rollback. I'll annotate when we hit one.
lee: ops-runbook-bot — link runbook for BMC rollback?
ops-runbook-bot: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/bmc-fw-rollback — follow section 4 (canary flash), section 7 for post-flash reprovision checks.
ashok: parallel: schedule rollback windows for affected models that cannot be config-fixed. Maria/eng-ml, can you estimate cost impact if we wait 2 hours vs 6 hours?
maria: rough: current burst to cloud is ~180 vGPU equivalents @ $0.40/hr -> ~ $72/hr, plus queue inefficiencies — with retries and spot churn we're at +$2.5k/hr as Jamie noted. If we fix via config now, cost drops to baseline in ~20–30m. If we need full rollback across 8 racks, expect 3–4 hours of extra disruption and ~ $6–9k incremental.
jamie: starting config push to canary racks now. I'll post progress.
lee: I'll coordinate with oncall to pause new cluster provisioning for eu-west3 via the scheduler gate to avoid further spillover. Use the temporary block rule: `scheduler.block(region=eu-west3,reason="bmc-firmware-reboots")`
oncall-bot: oncall escalated to eng-sre-rotation (next).
jamie: canary results: r05 (12 nodes) all stable after watchdog off. r06 (12 nodes) 10/12 stable, 2 nodes still rebooting — both are BMC-vX-mfg-abc which bmcctl reported "unsupported config".
maria: that matches the matrix. For those two models we need image rollback. I'll prepare rollback plan and get a small team to flash 2 racks at a time.  Estimated flash time per rack ~20m+validation.
nashok: decision: proceed with config roll for supported models across eu-west3 in 10m batches; simultaneously run coordinated rollback on unsupported racks in parallel (staggered) — try to finish within 4 hours. Escalate procurement if more flashing seats needed.
lee: please add emergency ratecap to autoscaler to limit cloud bursting while we fix: `autoscaler.set(burst_limit=100)` — prevents runaway cost.
jamie: applied autoscaler cap, confirmed burst reduced. Queue draining.
maria: starting rollback flash on eu-west3-r12 (first unsupported rack) — team A on it. Posting progress.
jamie: logs/troubleshooting notes saved to internal gist: https://internal.gists/3832109999-bmc-reboot-wave — includes ipmi dumps, affected node list, and per-rack model matrix.
lee: after-action items: 1) operator-facing firmware compatibility matrix needs to be published and enforced in deploy pipeline, 2) add a canary preflight that checks bmcctl apply-compat on a small sample before fleet rollout, 3) add metric for BMC watchdog resets to alert before bulk rollout.
maria: will send a short postmortem draft after stabilizing. Thanks everyone — critical fix in motion. :heart:
jamie: update 3832110400 — all config-fixed nodes stable, rollback flashes ongoing, autoscaler cost under control. Closing P1 when last unsupported racks finish flashing.
